provides: Admin-defined forms with anonymous responses: a workspace-keyed form whose schema is a list of stapel-attributes FeatureDefs, immutable published versions (every response records which schema it answered), two anonymous endpoints (fetch schema by non-enumerable public handle, submit answers) hardened by module-namespaced throttles, netintel-tiered captcha, size and volume caps and a recipient-side notify cooldown, capability-gated response review with streamed injection-safe CSV export, admin-initiated resend, ids-only form.* events, a GDPR provider and a finite retention purge.

curated.summary: The question types available to form authors. Ships as the ten builtin attribute kinds — text, number, yes/no, choice, date, section heading, colour, hierarchical choice, unit-bearing number. File uploads are absent by construction, not by omission: the platform's CDN cannot take custody of a stranger's bytes (no anonymous ingest, no auth-gated download), so a form attachment would be world-readable by URL. Widening this list is how a product adds its own question type after contributing it to stapel-attributes.
curated.business_label: What a form may ask for

curated.summary: Off, and it is a confession switch rather than a feature: a deployment with open public forms and no captcha backend gets a startup warning naming this setting. Turning it on silences the warning by saying the refusal is deliberate — which is a defensible position for an internal deployment and a bad surprise for a public one.
curated.business_label: Run public forms with no captcha

curated.summary: Off. The module does not persist a respondent's IP or browser string — rate limiting and network classification work off the live request and the cache, so nothing needs it on disk. A host that must keep abuse forensics turns it on, and that data then falls under the same retention clock as the answers themselves.

365 days, and finite is the point: anonymous respondents sit outside the platform's user-keyed erasure apparatus, so a bounded lifetime is the honest privacy mechanism rather than an implied promise. A form may shorten its own horizon; lengthening past the module ceiling requires raising the ceiling, so one form's settings cannot quietly rewrite the deployment's retention policy. Setting it to nothing keeps answers forever — an explicit choice a host makes, never the shipped default.

Zero. Publishing an edit mints a new immutable version, and a response in flight against the old one is refused wholesale so the renderer can refetch and tell the respondent the form changed — better than half-validating answers against a schema they never saw. A host that would rather accept the tail of in-flight fills opens a window here.
curated.business_label: Grace period after a form changes

extension_points.name: FIELD_KINDS
extension_points.summary: Which stapel-attributes kinds a form schema may use (default: the ten builtins). A host that registers a custom kind through STAPEL_ATTRIBUTES['EXTRA_TYPES'] or register_feature_type() adds it here to make it askable — registering a type somewhere in the process never by itself opens it to strangers on a public URL.

extension_points.name: attribute type registry
extension_points.summary: The field vocabulary itself is stapel-attributes' open registry, not a forms-local type system: a new question type is a type contribution there (config + DTO + DAO + validation), and it becomes server-validated in forms for free. The React pair mirrors it with registerFormFieldWidget.

extension_points.name: PRESENTERS
extension_points.summary: Every DTO is built by a presenter resolved through STAPEL_SWAP — swap keys FORMS_FORM_PRESENTER / FORMS_VERSION_PRESENTER / FORMS_SUBMISSION_PRESENTER reshape the form, version and response envelopes of every admin endpoint without forking a view. The anonymous envelope is deliberately not swappable: it is the one shape whose contents are a security decision.

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL.

surface.name: authorize
surface.intent: THE access decision for the admin surface. Returns allow|deny|unavailable (503, never 403-on-outage); fail-closed via workspaces.check_capability by comm name. Every new admin read or write routes through this — a second membership check is how a capability later ships half-enforced.

surface.name: csv_rows
surface.intent: One streamed, page-capped CSV export of a single version's responses, plus the keyset cursor for the next page. An export is the one read whose size is chosen by whoever filled the form in.

surface.name: escape_cell
surface.intent: Render a stored answer as a CSV-safe string, escaping the leading characters a spreadsheet would execute.

surface.name: export_filename
surface.intent: A safe attachment filename derived from the form title.
instead_of: putting an admin-authored title into Content-Disposition

surface.name: answer_columns
surface.intent: The (slug, label) columns of one version for review and export, section headings omitted. Stable per version — which is what the version FK buys.
instead_of: a union of columns over mutated schemas

surface.name: normalize_schema
surface.intent: Coerce an authored schema (full envelope or bare field list) into the stored shape, refusing anything else as a schema error rather than a 500 three layers down.
instead_of: indexing into a posted JSON body

surface.name: schema_fields
surface.intent: The field-def list of a stored schema, tolerant of anything already on disk.

surface.name: schema_meta
surface.intent: The form-level meta (title, description, confirmation text, submit label) of a stored schema.

surface.name: to_dao
surface.intent: Normalize validated answers into typed stored shapes. Never call it on unvalidated input: the engine's normalizer skips rather than refuses, so an invalid value would round-trip into storage.

surface.name: validate_answers
surface.intent: Validate a submitted answer set against a published schema, returning per-field errors that carry params.field plus the unknown slugs the attributes engine would have ignored. The engine is right to ignore them for listings and wrong for a public form.

surface.name: validate_schema
surface.intent: Refuse a draft that may not become a published version: field cap, kind allowlist, duplicate slugs, config keys the attributes dataclass would silently drop, then per-field config validity.

surface.name: create_form
surface.intent: Create a workspace-keyed form as a draft, with its non-enumerable public handle already minted and its retention override validated.

surface.name: delete_form
surface.intent: Soft-delete: intake stops immediately and rows survive for review until the retention purge cascades them.

surface.name: delete_submission
surface.intent: Destroy one response — the practical channel for an erasure request that arrives by email, until an email-keyed GDPR subject exists upstream.

surface.name: erase_user_submissions
surface.intent: Erase a user's answers while keeping the tombstone, so response counts and per-version analytics stay truthful.

surface.name: get_form
surface.intent: Fetch one live form inside a workspace scope — a form in another tenant, or in the trash, is a 404 rather than a row you have to remember to filter.

surface.name: get_submission
surface.intent: One response inside a workspace scope.

surface.name: list_forms
surface.intent: The workspace's live forms, newest first, optionally narrowed by state.

surface.name: list_submissions
surface.intent: Keyset page of a form's responses, newest first, capped service-side.

surface.name: publish
surface.intent: Validate the draft (caps, kind allowlist, duplicate slugs, silently-dropped config keys, per-field config validity) and freeze it as the next immutable version, atomically with the form.published emit.

surface.name: purge_deleted_forms
surface.intent: Destroy soft-deleted forms and everything under them, in the order the PROTECT constraint requires (answers before the versions they reference).

surface.name: purge_expired
surface.intent: Hard-delete responses past their retention horizon, honouring per-form overrides. After the horizon the count claim expires too, so these rows leave no tombstone.

surface.name: resend_submission
surface.intent: Re-deliver one response to the form's notify targets or to an explicit override. Not cooldown-gated: the cooldown suppresses a respondent-driven flood, and an operator asking for one letter is not one.

surface.name: resolve_public
surface.intent: Resolve a public handle with the uniform-404 discipline: unknown handle, soft-deleted form and draft are one byte-identical 404, while closed is 410 because that handle was public by definition and the renderer needs the difference.

surface.name: rotate_link
surface.intent: Mint a new public handle after a leak. Every distributed link dies and the row keeps its responses — which is the whole point of rotating rather than recreating.

surface.name: save_draft
surface.intent: Replace the builder's scratchpad. Deliberately permissive — a half-built form must be savable, and publish is the gate.

surface.name: set_state
surface.intent: Open or close a form for submissions: enforces the per-workspace open-form cap, refuses opening an unpublished form, and emits form.closed exactly once.

surface.name: submit
surface.intent: Accept one answered form: active-version check, volume cap, validation, normalization into typed storage and the ids-only event, all in one transaction. Nothing reaches disk that the version's own configs did not produce.

surface.name: update_form
surface.intent: Rename a form or replace its settings blob; the per-form retention override is checked against the module ceiling here, so one form's settings can never quietly rewrite the deployment's retention promise.

surface.name: get_forms_beat_schedule
surface.intent: The beat entry for the retention purge on the configured cadence, for a host to spread into CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE.
instead_of: hardcoding the task name and crontab in host settings

surface.name: purge_expired_submissions
surface.intent: The schedulable retention job: a plain callable, additionally a celery shared task under a stable name when celery is installed, logging what it destroyed. A retention policy nobody schedules is a promise, not a mechanism.
instead_of: a cron script calling into the ORM

requires.reason: comm bus (form.* Actions, the workspaces.check_capability client), JWT authentication, unified error envelope, netintel-tiered captcha, notification publishing, GDPR provider registry, staff-mandate declarations, AppSettings config layer
the field vocabulary IS this library's FeatureDef registry, and every submission is validated and normalized by its pipeline — forms defines no field types of its own

every admin request asks the workspaces.check_capability comm Function (fail-closed, deny-by-default) — stapel-workspaces is the shelf's answerer; any provider of that Function satisfies the contract, and without one the admin surface denies while the public respondent endpoints keep working

notify-on-submit and resend request notifications through stapel-core; without a notifications service the rows are still stored and the events still emitted, but nobody is told. The forms.submission_received / forms.submission_resend routing entries must exist there (or in the host's STAPEL_NOTIFICATIONS['TYPES'])
the FormsGDPRProvider registers itself for authenticated respondents; hosts must also list "forms" in STAPEL_GDPR['DATA_OWNERS'] or the erasure closure never completes (check stapel_forms.W003)
